extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders and the public (regulated entities, state agencies, attorneys, and interested commenters) interested in EPA's proposed SIP revision for Florida
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register proposed rule by EPA to approve a Florida SIP revision removing obsolete CAIR-related definitions; the document sets legal standards for approval and gives procedural instructions for submitting public comments by a fixed deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received on or before April 28, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit by the stated date to ensure consideration. See the DATES section for the official deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments / docket identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your comments, identified by Docket ID No. EPA-R04-OAR-2024-0049 at regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions for submitting comments on Regulations.gov. For additional submission methods and the full EPA public comment policy, visit https://www.epa.gov/dockets/commenting-epa-dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: No editing or removal after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed from Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful to include final content; plan submissions accordingly. EPA may publish comments; submissions may not be viewable until agency approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBI and other restricted disclosures should not be placed in the public docket. Follow EPA guidance on handling CBI for alternate submission methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written comment is considered the official comment and should include discussion of all points you wish to make.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary submission requirement (no external locations)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on links to external sites as a substitute for placing material in the official docket; include substantive material in the Regulations.gov submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA publication and redaction of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may publish any comment received to its public docket. Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them. Assume public disclosure unless you follow EPA's CBI procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good neighbor (interstate transport) legal standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CAA section 110(a)(2)(D)(i)(I), also called the 'good neighbor' provision, states are required to address the interstate transport of air pollution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, each state's implementation plan must contain adequate provisions to prohibit emissions that will significantly contribute to nonattainment of the NAAQS, or that will interfere with maintenance of the NAAQS, in any other state. This is the substantive statutory standard applicable to SIP provisions addressing interstate transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIP approval standard (EPA's role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the CAA, the Administrator is required to approve a SIP submission that complies with the provisions of the CAA and applicable Federal regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's role is to approve state choices, provided that they meet the criteria of the CAA; EPA will not impose additional requirements beyond those imposed by state law in this action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-interference requirement (CAA section 110(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: CAA section 110(l) prohibits EPA from approving a SIP revision that would interfere with any applicable requirement concerning attainment and reasonable further progress (as defined in CAA Section 171), or any other applicable requirement of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluated whether removing CAIR-related definitions would interfere with attainment or other CAA requirements and concluded it would not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is proposing to include in a final EPA rule regulatory text that includes incorporation by reference in accordance with requirements of 1 CFR 51.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposes to incorporate by reference Florida Rule 62-210.200 (state-effective on specified dates) except for enumerated exclusions; EPA will make the materials generally available through regulations.gov and at the EPA Region 4 office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of action limited to specified state-effective changes
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is proposing to approve only the changes that became state-effective on July 3, 2018; other revisions in the August 15, 2023 submittal will be acted on in separate rulemakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenting or assessing the proposal, focus on the specific definitions and paragraph changes identified as part of this action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-application on Indian reservation land / tribal implications
rubrics_metrics.description: The SIP is not approved to apply on any Indian reservation land or in any other area where EPA or an Indian tribe has demonstrated that a tribe has jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In those areas of Indian country, the rule does not have Tribal implications and will not impose substantial direct costs on Tribal governments or preempt Tribal law as specified by Executive Order 13175.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review / statutory certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed action: is not a significant regulatory action under Executive Order 12866; does not impose an information collection burden under the Paperwork Reduction Act; is certified as not having a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the Regulatory Flexibility Act; does not contain unfunded mandates, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These certifications explain that EPA considers this action to be an approvable state-law-alignment action with limited regulatory-economic effects; commenters may address these determinations if relevant.
